1. Dataset Description
	I will be using an excerpt from ‘Y Gododdin’ a middle welsh poem about a Saxon defeat of the Britons during the battle of Cattraith, ca. 600 CE. The full poem is quite long so I will be using just the first 18 sections (around 968 words). I was able to find a transcription online here (https://www.maryjones.us/ctexts/a01w.html) that I can easily copy into a .txt file. For a more serious citation, the text appears in The Four Ancient Books of Wales. ed. by William F. Skene. Edinburgh: Edmonston and Douglas, 1868.(https://archive.org/details/fourancientbooks01skenuoft/mode/2up)
2. Rationale
      I choose this dataset because I found the historical context interesting and because it was easily found in a copy-and-paste-able format. Linguistically I find the way that welsh uses the Latin alphabet very interesting. Welsh has more sounds that the Latin alphabet does characters and the way that they use two characters to represent one sound goes farther than just the English “sh” or “th”.
3. Type of Analysis 
      I will be using frequency analysis for overall information about sound appearances, pattern matching for gaining phonotactic information. I will be counting and comparing the sounds present in the text, with a focus on /ɬ/ because it sounds neat.
4. Preliminary Questions
    • What phonotactic rules does the welsh “ll” (/ɬ/ )follow?
    • Do the same rules apply to “l”? 
        ◦ I expect to find that similar phonotactic rules apply to both due to their phonological similarity
    • Can I find any patterns that determine when “l” is used compared to “ll” ?
    • bonus: Can I find any patterns that determine when “d” is used compared to “dd” (/d/ vs /ð/)?
